:::{#exr-transpose-product-practice}
#### The order of the factors in a transposed square product

@rem-transpose-product-order shows that,
for factors that are not [square](#def-square-matrix),
keeping the original order of the factors in the [transpose](#def-matrix-transpose) of a [product](#def-matrix-mult) can give an undefined product.
For two [square matrices](#def-square-matrix) of the same size,
both $\tp{\matr{A}}\tp{\matr{B}}$ and $\tp{\matr{B}}\tp{\matr{A}}$ are defined,
so the shapes alone cannot settle which order gives $\tp{(\matr{A}\matr{B})}$.
Let

$$
\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix},
\qquad
\matr{B} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}.
$$

Does $\tp{\matr{A}}\tp{\matr{B}}$ equal $\tp{(\matr{A}\matr{B})}$ for these $\matr{A}$ and $\matr{B}$?

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Hint

Compute $\matr{A}\matr{B}$ with @def-matrix-mult and take its [transpose](#def-matrix-transpose),
then compute $\tp{\matr{A}}\tp{\matr{B}}$ and compare the two entry by entry.

:::
